data.narrative:
Longshot Space is a seed-stage aerospace company founded by Mike Grace and Nathan Saichek that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 13 comparable companies spanning public equities (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and private firms including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach given data constraints. Using the $10M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $25M. Peer-median analysis could not be applied due to insufficient data density; while 14 same-sector peers exist, none of the narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier) produced the minimum three comparable datapoints required for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples is not feasible without disclosed target revenue, though the sector median of 27.4x P/S across five public Space & Aerospace names provides directional context.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, centered on $25M. This range reflects moderate confidence given the single-method derivation. Key uncertainties include the absence of a robust private peer set at seed stage within aerospace, lack of revenue visibility, and the methodological reliance on stage-based multipliers rather than fundamental comparables. Additional revenue or customer traction data would enable public-comp anchoring and strengthen conviction.
